pr_comments:
Hey there @mletenay, mind taking a look at this pull request as it has been labeled with an integration (`goodwe`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L409) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
@starkillerOG the `async_reset` is the function to be called by `async_track_point_in_time`, it's fine to pass a `@callback` to it 👍

Tested and it works with my GW3600D-NS invertor (no home battery).
@emontnemery would you be see kind to review/merge again?

@starkillerOG I still don't understand how your patch works since you're just overwriting the API data.

You write:
> The update coordinator will fail since the inverter is offline at night, and the previous value will be reported which is also set to 0 during reset, so the value will continue to be 0.

OK, so the value remains at 0 while the device is offline - until it wakes up again in the morning.
What happens when the device wakes up the next morning, it knows it's a new day, and resets the relevant reading to 0?

@emontnemery Yes as long as the sun is under the inverter does not have power and will not respond. When it wakes up in the morning at first light it knows it is a new day and will start with values of 0 for daily production. So the first responses of the inverter will equal the 0 we set at midnight. Then during the day the daily production value will rise untill sunset in the evening and the inverter will go offline. HomeAssistant will then keep reporting the last known value untill midnight.

Here is the history of the relevant entity for 2 days when the patch is not applied:
![Daily production](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14811189/189866014-9c14b37b-bea7-461c-b3d2-66158e81edba.PNG)

What we are basically doing is chaning the reset to 0 from the moment the inverter wakes up to a fixed time: midnight.

@starkillerOG OK, thanks for the patience with explaining 👍

My concern is that the reset forced by Home Assistant may not be synchronized with the inverter itself, meaning you could potentially have this sequence:
- Home Assistant resets the value to 0
- The inverter sends another update with the total of the day
- The inverter resets the value to 0 next morning

If this happens, Home Assistant will count the daily production twice.
Maybe this can happen if the user reboots the inverter after midnight, or if the inverter and Home Assistant are not using the same time zones?

@emontnemery there is a check that ensures the reset only takes place if the inverter is "unavailable" at the moment of reset (in case the invertor is connected to a Home Battery and has power during midnight). I think it is safe to say that at midnight it will be dark around the world (except maybe fore the northpole or something), so the inverter will not have power and will not report any values.

The timezone of the invert schould be synchronized to HomeAssistant (in the new release there will be a button entity to synchronize the HomeAssistant time with the inverter: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/69220).
If they are not synchronized and the invertor is online during midnight when the times are out of sync the problem you discribed can occur even withouth HomeAssistant reseting the value to 0.

Users can't reboot the inverter at midnight because the inverter is completly dead without solar power, if solar power drops below the minimum required value the invertor disconnects itself from the grid and will therefore be completly withouth power when the sun is down. (buttons on the invert will not do anything).

@starkillerOG Oh, so the inverter is not powered by mains, it's self powered by the connected solar panels? In that case it should indeed be fine 👍

You could otherwise consider to expose the offending sensors, a "raw" version which is guaranteed to not break statistics, and a filtered version which does a best effort attempt to reset at midnight. Only the raw sensor should set state_class to `total_increasing`.
@emontnemery there is already a `e_total` sensor which is always just increasing and which is used for the energy dashboard. This sensor is not effected by this PR.

issue_context.title: GoodWe inverter integration doesn't reset Today's Generation on start of day
issue_context.body: ### The problem With the latest change to this integration (https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/69218) the 'totals' are not reset at the start of the day but only when the value changes. This _may_ be OK for when the inverter is offline due to no PV generation, but as soon as the inverter starts generating the value of at least 'Today's Generation' should be reset to 0. Especially on smaller inverters where it takes a long time for the inverter to reach the first 0.1 kWh it is strange that the integration still reports the generation of yesterday... This shows current PV power. As you can see it starts generating at about 7:15 AM This shows Today's Generation. As you can see it's still reporting yesterday's value ### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? 2022.7.5 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? _No response_ ### What type of installation are you running? Home Assistant OS ### Integration causing the issue goodwe ### Link to integration documentation on our website https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/goodwe ### Diagnostics information _No response_ ### Example YAML snippet _No response_ ### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us? _No response_ ### Additional information _No response_

<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

@mletenay maybe we can schedule a function call at 00:00 each night to set the value back to 0?
We can maybe use `async_track_point_in_time` form `homeassistant.helpers.event`.
Use `async_added_to_hass` from the Todays generation entity to issue the first `async_track_point_in_time` and then in the function that resets the value schedule the next `async_track_point_in_time`.
Then in the `async_will_remove_from_hass` we can cancell the `async_track_point_in_time` to clean up.
